strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial improvements in specificity (43.2 points over AlphaEdit on LLaMA-3-8B) while maintaining high efficacy, consistently across three model architectures

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (COUNTERFACT, zsRE), diverse metrics (efficacy, generalization, specificity, fluency, consistency, general capability), and robustness tests (CHED, 5000-edit scalability)

Thorough analysis section with clear evidence for core hypotheses: last-token perturbation reduction (Section 6.1), entity-specific vs. entity-agnostic feature decomposition (Section 6.2.1), and critical subspace identification (Section 6.2.2)
Well-grounded methodology leveraging Linear Representation Hypothesis with reasonable assumptions about semantic feature decomposition
Strong reproducibility: promised code/data release, comprehensive hyperparameter documentation, and detailed experimental protocol
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (heatmaps, component analysis, tradeoff curves) and well-structured ablation study demonstrating synergy between components
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (SVD-based subspace identification, energy thresholding, subspace constraints) are standard techniques; primary contribution is their application to AlphaEdit, which is somewhat incremental

2D subspace assumption for residual vector δ' lacks strong justification: authors acknowledge w1 and w2 are not fully disentangled (Section 6.2.2), no ablation on dimensionality choice, and theoretical motivation is weakened by post-hoc validation via Table 4

Subspace analysis could be stronger: variance analysis (Table 2) shows only 2.6x-4.5x differences, and the claim that K⊥ₛ captures entity-agnostic features is validated indirectly through variance rather than direct validation of feature semantics

Simplified modeling choices: ignoring w1-w2 interactions (Appendix C) and assuming dimensionality without systematic justification reduce theoretical rigor, though empirical results suggest pragmatic validity

Scope limitations: only addresses MLP down-projection editing within locate-then-edit paradigm; unclear applicability to other editing methods (attention heads, LoRA) or knowledge types beyond Wikidata factual knowledge

Missing ablations and analyses: no comparison of subspace constraints applied to other baselines (RECT, PRUNE), unclear if per-model hyperparameter tuning would improve results, no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
General capability degradation on some benchmarks (Table 8 shows near-zero F1 on select GPT-J/Qwen tasks) suggests potential side effects that deserve further investigation
Hyperparameter choices fixed across models without sensitivity validation: τenergy=0.4 and λ=0.3 held constant despite Figure 5 showing clear tradeoffs; unclear if these are optimal or require tuning
